findings.title: upsampled_count does not default missing or zero sample_weight to 1
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. In Snuba, `sample_weight` is only populated for events ingested with a `sample_rate`; for unsampled error events, events ingested before client error sampling was enabled on the project, or events from SDKs that do not send `client_sample_rate`, `sample_weight` is `NULL` or `0`. Summing `sample_weight` directly without defaulting unset values to `1` (e.g., `if(sample_weight > 0, sample_weight, 1)` or `greatest(ifNull(sample_weight, 1), 1)`) causes unsampled events in allowlisted projects to contribute `0` instead of `1` to the total error count.

findings.title: Allowlist cache uses process-salted hash() and serves stale results when options change
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist check in `sentry.utils.cache.cache` for 60 seconds using `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` in the cache key. In Python 3, `hash()` is randomized per process via `PYTHONHASHSEED`, so different worker processes compute different cache keys for the same `project_ids` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` cannot invalidate entries written by other processes. Moreover, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is updated, `sentry.options.get` already caches option lookups, and this cache causes stale results in production as well as test pollution when `options.get` is mocked with different values for the same organization and project IDs.

findings.title: _get_event_stats passes outer dataset and request instead of scoped_dataset and query
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, ...)`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the outer `dataset` variable and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query from `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance` into `discover` with a modified `query` (such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`), the upsampling check evaluates the original outer `dataset` and `request.GET["query"]` rather than the actual dataset and query being executed.

findings.title: _is_error_focused_query matches negated and mixed event.type queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` via a plain substring check. This returns `True` for negated queries like `!event.type:error` (which explicitly exclude errors to query transactions) and mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, causing `count()` to be replaced with `upsampled_count()` on non-error events.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink sentry-repo committed to repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`) without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This appears to be an accidentally committed nested git repository and will cause `git submodule` commands in CI and developer checkouts to fail.

findings.title: Unrelated change to topEvents validation error message
findings.body: The validation error message for `top_events <= 0` was changed from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`, which is unrelated to error upsampling and can break existing tests or clients expecting the previous message.
